beginner_intro: Al-Ikhlas is only four short verses, but the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) described it as equal in meaning to a third of the Quran, because it summarises the entire Islamic concept of God's Oneness (Tawhid) — see Lesson 1, "Who is Allah?". Many Muslims recite it daily; it is short enough for a beginner to memorise in one sitting.

translations.text: Say, He is Allah, [who is] One,

tafsirs.text_summary: The surah opens as an instruction to Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare God's absolute Oneness in response to those who asked him to describe God — a direct, unambiguous answer rather than a comparison to anything already known.
"As-Samad" describes God as the One all creation depends on and turns to in need, while He depends on nothing and no one — the reverse of every other relationship a person experiences.

translations.text: He neither begets nor is born,

tafsirs.text_summary: A direct statement that God has no offspring and was not born of anything — addressing, among other things, the divine sonship claimed for other figures in some other traditions, and affirming instead that God is uncreated and without succession.

translations.text: Nor is there to Him any equivalent.

tafsirs.text_summary: Closes the surah with the widest possible statement: nothing at all is comparable or equal to God — in essence, in attributes, or in right to be worshipped.
